q: Which of the following are not full UN member states: Palestine or Vatican City?
ans: Neither is a full UN member in the same sense: Palestine is a non-member observer State; the Holy See (associated with Vatican City) is a non-member observer
facts: • The United Nations has 193 member states.
“Holy See” is the UN observer entity, while “Vatican City” is the state; wording should be precise.

q: Which countries are known as the Baltic states?
facts: • All three border the Baltic Sea.
Their capitals are Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius, respectively.

q: Which party did Quaid-e-Azam join before joining the Muslim League?
ans: Indian National Congress (joined in 1906); he joined the Muslim League in 1913
facts: • Jinnah initially supported Hindu-Muslim cooperation.
He later became the leading figure in the movement for Pakistan.

q: In which Hijri year did Hazrat Khalid bin al-Walid (RA) accept Islam?
ans: 8 AH (commonly dated before the conquest of Makkah)
facts: • Khalid became one of the most successful commanders in early Islamic history.
He is traditionally known as Sayf Allah (“Sword of Allah”).

q: Which country has a border of “1,200 miles” with Pakistan?
ans: Unclear as written; the country and measurement are not specified, so no safe single answer can be verified
facts: • Pakistan's major land neighbours are India, Afghanistan, Iran and China.
The Durand Line with Afghanistan is often cited at about 2,640 km, but published lengths vary.

q: In which battle were about 70 Muslim Companions martyred?
facts: • Traditional accounts commonly report about 70 Muslim martyrs at Uhud.
The battle took place in 3 AH / 625 CE.

q: What is the title “Kalimullah” associated with which prophet?
facts: • Kalimullah means “the one who spoke with Allah” in Islamic tradition.
Musa (AS) is also associated with the Torah.

q: What is Pakistan's national flower?
facts: • Jasmine is the commonly recognized national flower of Pakistan.
The national tree is commonly listed as the Deodar cedar.

q: How often does a leap year usually occur?
ans: Every 4 years, with Gregorian calendar exceptions
facts: • A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400.
For example, 2000 was a leap year, but 1900 was not.

q: In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered?
facts: • The conquest took place in Ramadan 8 AH.
It followed the breach of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and resulted in the entry into Makkah with limited fighting.

q: How many months have 31 days?
facts: • They are January, March, May, July, August, October and December.
February has 28 days in a common year and 29 in a leap year.

q: What period is associated with the Montagu–Chelmsford reforms?
ans: The 1918 report and the Government of India Act 1919
facts: • The Act introduced dyarchy in provincial government.
It expanded Indian participation but retained substantial British control.

q: A light-year is a unit of what?
facts: • A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres.
It is not a unit of time despite the word “year.”

q: In which year did the Indian War of Independence/revolt occur?
facts: • The uprising began at Meerut in May 1857 and spread across parts of northern India.
British colonial histories often called it the Indian Mutiny; Indian narratives commonly call it the First War of Independence.

q: When did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan establish the Scientific Society?
facts: • The Society aimed to translate modern scientific works into Indian languages.
It later moved to Aligarh.

q: Which work did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan write in response to William Muir's biography of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
ans: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya (published in the early 1870s; dates vary by edition)
facts: • Sir Syed's work responded to criticisms of the Prophet's life.
William Muir published his biography of Muhammad in 1858–1861.

q: When did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan establish the MAO School at Aligarh?
facts: • The school became Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1877.
The college later developed into Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: When was the Indian National Congress founded by A.O. Hume and others?
facts: • The first Congress session was held in Bombay in December 1885.
A.O. Hume was a British civil servant who helped organize the meeting with Indian leaders.

q: When was the Partition of Bengal announced/implemented?
facts: • The partition was announced under Viceroy Lord Curzon and took effect in October 1905.
It was annulled in 1911 amid strong political opposition.

q: When did the Simla Deputation take place?
facts: • Muslim leaders met Viceroy Lord Minto at Simla on 1 October 1906.
The deputation sought separate electorates and political safeguards for Muslims.

q: When was the All-India Muslim League founded in Dhaka?
facts: • The organization later became central to the Pakistan Movement.
Its founding occurred during the annual meeting of the Muhammadan Educational Conference.

q: When were the Morley–Minto reforms enacted?
facts: • The Indian Councils Act 1909 is known as the Morley–Minto reforms.
It introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

q: When was the Partition of Bengal annulled?
ans: 1911 (announced at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December)
facts: • The province's partition had begun in 1905.
The capital of British India was also announced to be shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam join the All-India Muslim League?
facts: • He had joined the Indian National Congress in 1906.
Jinnah's political career initially emphasized constitutional reform and Hindu-Muslim cooperation.

q: When was the Lucknow Pact signed?
facts: • The agreement was between the Indian National Congress and the All-India Muslim League.
It recognized separate electorates and an agreed scheme of political representation.

q: When did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre occur?
facts: • It occurred in Amritsar, Punjab, during British rule.
Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to fire on a gathering.

q: When did the Khilafat Movement take place?
facts: • The movement sought to preserve the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
It overlapped with Gandhi's Non-Cooperation Movement in India.

q: When was the Nehru Report published?
facts: • It was chaired by Motilal Nehru.
Jinnah's Fourteen Points in 1929 responded to major provisions of the report.

q: When were Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points presented?
facts: • They set out demands for constitutional safeguards for Muslims.
The points included federalism, provincial autonomy and representation.

q: When did Allama Iqbal deliver the Allahabad Address?
facts: • The address was delivered at the Muslim League session on 29 December 1930.
It is often associated with the idea of a consolidated Muslim-majority region in northwestern India.

q: When were the Round Table Conferences held in London?
facts: • There were three conferences.
They discussed constitutional reforms for British India; Congress attended the second conference but not the first or third as a delegation.

q: When did Congress ministries govern provincial administrations before resigning?
facts: • Congress ministries formed after the 1937 provincial elections.
They resigned in 1939 after the Viceroy declared India at war without consulting Indian leaders.

q: When was the Day of Deliverance observed by the Muslim League?
facts: • It followed the resignation of Congress provincial ministries.
Muhammad Ali Jinnah asked Muslims to observe the day after the resignations.

q: When was the Lahore Resolution passed?
facts: • It was adopted at the Muslim League session in Lahore on 23 March.
It called for independent states in Muslim-majority zones; it later became popularly known as the Pakistan Resolution.

q: When did the Cripps Mission visit India?
facts: • Sir Stafford Cripps arrived in March 1942 during World War II.
The mission's constitutional proposals were rejected by major Indian political groups.

q: When did the Gandhi–Jinnah talks take place?
facts: • The talks were held in Bombay in September 1944.
They failed to agree on the Pakistan demand and the mechanics of partition.

q: When was the Wavell Plan proposed?
facts: • The plan proposed reconstituting the Viceroy's Executive Council.
It was discussed at the Simla Conference in June–July 1945.

q: When was the Simla Conference held?
facts: • Viceroy Lord Wavell convened it to discuss the Executive Council.
The conference broke down over the Muslim League's claim to nominate all Muslim members.

q: When were elections to the central and provincial legislatures of British India held before independence?
facts: • The elections were a major political test for the Congress and Muslim League.
The Muslim League won most Muslim-reserved seats, strengthening its claim to represent Muslim voters.

q: When was the Cabinet Mission sent to India?
facts: • The mission comprised Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.
Its plan proposed a united India with a weak centre and provincial groupings, but agreement collapsed.

q: When was the 3 June Plan announced?
facts: • The plan set out the partition of British India into India and Pakistan.
It was announced by Mountbatten and accepted by major political leaders with qualifications.

q: On what date did Pakistan become independent?
facts: • Pakistan's Independence Day is observed on 14 August.
The transfer of power and the Indian Independence Act were tied to the end of British rule in August 1947.

q: How many administrative divisions did Punjab have in the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • Administrative counts can change as new districts/divisions are notified.
For an exam asking “current” counts, use the latest official Punjab government list rather than an undated MCQ sheet. Primary / official reference

q: How many divisions did Sindh have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • The 2023 census administrative table listed six divisions in Sindh.
Division and district counts can change after administrative notifications. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 60

q: How many divisions did Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • The commonly listed divisions are Malakand, Hazara, Mardan, Peshawar, Kohat, Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan.
Merged former FATA districts are administered within KP divisions. Primary / official reference

q: How many divisions did Balochistan have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • The 2023 census table listed eight divisions.
Balochistan is Pakistan's largest province by area. Primary / official reference

q: How many divisions did Pakistan have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • The PBS 2023 table also counted 136 districts including Islamabad Capital Territory.
These are dated census baseline numbers, not a guarantee that no later administrative changes occurred. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 61

q: How many districts did Punjab have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • The count in a later administrative list may differ because provinces can create districts.
Punjab is Pakistan's most populous province. Primary / official reference

q: How many districts did Sindh have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • Karachi is administratively divided into multiple districts.
Manchar is Pakistan's largest natural freshwater lake and Keenjhar is an artificial reservoir, both in Sindh. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 62

q: How many districts did Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
ans: 35 districts in the PBS table; some government lists have shown 34, so cite the reference year/source
facts: • District totals are especially sensitive to newly notified districts and merged areas.
For exam use, memorize the count only with its source date. Primary / official reference

q: How many districts did Balochistan have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • New district notifications can change this total.
Chagai is commonly listed as the largest district of Balochistan by area. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 63

q: How many districts are in Islamabad Capital Territory in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • Islamabad Capital Territory is federally administered and is not one of Pakistan's four provinces.
The national capital is Islamabad. Primary / official reference

q: How many districts did Pakistan have in the PBS 2023 Census baseline?
facts: • The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics published the count in its 2023 census administrative table.
Because boundaries change between censuses, always cite the reference year for such figures. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 64

q: What was Najashi's religion before the traditional account of his acceptance of Islam?
facts: • Najashi was the ruler of Abyssinia who gave protection to Muslim migrants.
The first migration to Abyssinia took place before the Hijrah to Madinah.

q: What is the currency of Indonesia?
facts: • Jakarta has long been Indonesia's principal capital city; Indonesia is developing Nusantara as a new capital.
The rupiah is abbreviated IDR.

q: Who was the mother of Prophet Ismail (AS)?
facts: • Hajra and Ismail (AS) are associated with Makkah and the well of Zamzam in Islamic tradition.
Prophet Ibrahim (AS) is Ismail's father.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the men's Hockey World Cup associated with its 1990s title?
facts: • Pakistan won the Men's Hockey World Cup in Sydney in 1994.
Pakistan also won the Champions Trophy in 1994; the men's World Cup was not won by Pakistan in 1995. Primary / official reference

q: Who wrote the Punjabi qissa “Sohni Mahiwal”?
ans: Fazal Shah is traditionally credited with a famous Punjabi version; versions vary
facts: • Sohni Mahiwal is a classic Punjabi tragic romance.
Like Heer Ranjha, it has multiple oral and literary versions.

q: Who wrote “Kashf-ul-Mahjoob”?
ans: Ali ibn Usman al-Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)
facts: • The book is an important early treatise on Sufism written in Persian.
Al-Hujwiri's shrine is in Lahore.

q: Who won the 1999 ICC Cricket World Cup?
facts: • The final was played at Lord's in London on 20 June 1999.
Australia defeated Pakistan in the final of the 1999 edition. Primary / official reference

q: Where is NATO headquarters located?
facts: • NATO was established on 4 April 1949.
The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington, D.C. Primary / official reference

q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA)?
facts: • Hafsa (RA) was among the Prophet's wives known as the Mothers of the Believers.
She is associated in traditional accounts with custody of an early written collection of Qur'anic material after Abu Bakr and Umar.

q: Who is commonly cited as the youngest Nishan-e-Haider recipient?
facts: • Rashid Minhas was 20 years old when he sacrificed his life in 1971.
His action took place during the 1971 war and involved preventing an aircraft from being taken to India.

q: Who was Pakistan's first Commander-in-Chief of the Army?
facts: • Messervy took office at independence in August 1947.
General Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief in 1951.

q: Who first built the Kaaba?
ans: Islamic traditions differ; the Qur'an clearly says Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) raised its foundations (2:127)
facts: • Some traditional narratives say Adam (AS) first built it, but that is not established explicitly in the Qur'anic verse.
For a scripture-grounded exam answer, remember Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) rebuilding/raising the foundations.

q: What is another name for the Manila Pact?
ans: Southeast Asia Collective Defense Treaty; associated with SEATO
facts: • The pact was signed in 1954.
SEATO was dissolved in 1977.

q: When was the Qibla changed from Jerusalem toward the Kaaba?
ans: 2 AH / about 624 CE, after the Hijrah
facts: • The change is traditionally placed around 16–18 months after the migration to Madinah.
The direction of prayer is toward the Kaaba in Makkah.

q: What was Faisalabad formerly called?
facts: • The city was renamed Faisalabad in 1977 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.
It is a major textile and industrial centre of Pakistan.

q: Which is commonly listed as Pakistan's most populous district?
ans: Lahore District (according to the 2023 census comparison; check later boundary changes)
facts: • Karachi is Pakistan's largest city, but its population is divided among several districts.
District and city population rankings are not the same.

q: Who proposed the idea that led to the formation of SAARC?
ans: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh is commonly credited with proposing regional cooperation in 1980
facts: • SAARC was formally established in Dhaka in December 1985.
Its founding members included Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

q: How many books are included in the Sunni Kutub al-Sittah (six canonical hadith collections)?
facts: • They include Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Sunan al-Nasa'i and Sunan Ibn Majah.
“Kutub al-Sittah” means the six books.

q: Who killed Hazrat Hamza (RA) at the Battle of Uhud, according to traditional Islamic accounts?
facts: • Hamza (RA) was the Prophet's paternal uncle and a prominent early Muslim.
Wahshi later accepted Islam according to traditional accounts.
